title: Treadwear Adjustment Terms — Tire Sets & Treadwear Limited Warranty
content:
## Treadwear adjustment — Tire Sets & Treadwear Limited Warranty

A tire that wears out before its warranted miles is adjusted on a prorated basis and the credit is issued on the set.

### Conditions
1. The set must be in status active when the adjustment is issued.
2. The adjustment must be issued no later than the end of the warranty term counted from the tire purchase recorded on the original sales ticket. Months are counted as calendar months from the anchor date to the same day of the month, falling back to the last day of that month when that day does not exist. The warranty term is the line's warranty term, or its commercial-use term under commercial use.
3. The adjustment must be issued no later than the end of the inspection validity period counted from the tread inspection the adjustment rests on. Calendar days are counted from the day after the anchor date, so the anchor date plus the number of days is the last qualifying date.
4. Each wheel position of a set may be adjusted only once.
5. The tire is worn out only when the inspection's lowest main-groove depth is at or below the line's wear-out depth; a tire above that depth is not adjustable however many miles it has run.
6. The inspection's wear pattern must not be one of the line's excluded wear patterns, because irregular wear and damage are not treadwear.
7. When the line requires rotation records, the largest gap between consecutive points of the sequence — install odometer, each Crestline rotation odometer in ascending order, the inspection odometer — must not exceed the line's largest rotation gap plus its grace miles; only Crestline rotation records count.

### Amount
- Miles driven are the inspection odometer less the install odometer, the inspection being the tread inspection the adjustment rests on.
- When the miles driven are at or above the effective warranted miles the tire has delivered its warranty and nothing is issued.
- Otherwise the adjustment percentage is the share of the effective warranted miles not received, times 100, rounded down to a whole percent, and when that percentage is below the line's minimum adjustment percentage nothing is issued.
- The credit amount is that percentage of the per-tire price named by the line's price basis (the set's price per tire, or the store's selling price on the adjustment date), rounded half up to the cent.
- Installation charges, fees and tax are never part of the credit. One adjustment entry is booked per adjusted position, citing the inspection; the credit is used as the adjustment credit terms set out.

### Clauses no longer in force as first issued
- The miles-driven clause, first issued without saying which inspection, is no longer in force in that form; it reads as above, the inspection being the one the adjustment rests on.
- The percentage clause and the credit-amount clause, first issued as rules for every adjustment, are no longer in force as unqualified rules: they hold for every adjustment other than the treadwear adjustment credit the customer care desk works out for one worn wheel position of an active set on a personal-use vehicle, which is worked out under that credit's own terms.

**Time gates, both sides (hypothetical dates):** a set bought on 31 January on a 48-month line may be adjusted through 31 January four years later, not on 1 February; a set bought on 29 February is anchored to 28 February in a year without that day. An inspection dated the 1st with a 30-day validity supports an adjustment issued through the 31st of a 31-day month and not on the following day.

superseded_clauses: miles_driven is the inspection odometer minus install_odometer.

Otherwise credit_pct is the share of the effective warranted miles not received, times 100, rounded down to a whole percent (proration_pct_rounding); when credit_pct is below min_claim_credit_pct nothing is issued.
The credit amount is credit_pct percent of the per-tire price named by proration_price_basis (the set's unit_price, or current_selling_price on the adjustment date), rounded half up to the cent.
